Aussie interest rate expectations rocket, signalling potential RBA hawkish pivot amid sticky inflation
Qantas ground crews vote for strike action, threatening QAN.AX operations and consumer confidence
Star Entertainment (STAR.AX) bleeds $307m as auditors raise going-concern doubts
Iron ore sentiment weakens ('roaches seeth'), pressuring BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX
Australia flagged as risking AI economic boom due to slow corporate uptake
Rare earths and gold exploration activity intensifies: Lindian, Barkly, Great Southern, Kaiser all advancing projects
Property investor credit growth crashes post-budget tax changes, amplifying REIT and property developer stress

sectors.trend: Iron ore sentiment weakens amid demand concerns; gold and rare earths exploration activity accelerates with multiple WA/NT projects advancing
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face headwinds from soft iron ore; gold miners (GOLD.AX, NVG.AX) and rare earths (LRE.AX, LND.AX) benefit from diversification and strategic mineral demand

sectors.trend: Rising rate expectations support NIMs but property credit stress and investor lending crash threaten asset quality; Macquarie (MQG.AX) audit bid adds governance noise
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX benefit from higher rates but face rising NPL risk from property downturn; MQG.AX faces competitive audit pressure

sectors.trend: Oil spikes on Hormuz tensions; One Nation pushes coal/nuclear in Victoria; wind farm drought persists; oil giant retreats from clean energy
sectors.implications: WDS.AX, WLE.AX, SXG.AX gain from oil price; renewable names (LXG.AX, IGN.AX) face policy uncertainty; Danish entrant may revive wind pipeline

sectors.trend: Severe downturn: home values decline sharply, buyer activity at lows, auction sentiment deteriorates, Bathla near insolvency, investor credit crashes
sectors.implications: REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX, DGL.AX) face falling valuations and occupancy risk; property developers (BVH.AX, STG.AX) under severe stress; insurers (CGU.AX, WPA.AX) face claims pressure

sectors.trend: Qantas strike vote threatens operations; Woolworths drops Tassie beef; EV uptake accelerates; weight-loss drug demand surges
sectors.implications: QAN.AX faces operational and reputational risk; WES.AX, WOW.AX affected by supply chain shifts; CSL.AX benefits from weight-loss drug demand

sectors.trend: Australia flagged as slow AI adopter; Meta $24b settlement influenced by AU social media ban; global AI infrastructure buildout continues
sectors.implications: ASX tech names (W1.AX, XRO.AX) face competitive disadvantage; regulatory action on Meta signals AU policy leadership but limited domestic AI infrastructure

Australian property credit cycle turning sharply negative
RBA rate expectations rising, pressuring growth stocks
Strategic minerals (rare earths, gold, uranium) exploration boom

Energy policy fragmentation (coal vs renewables vs nuclear)

risk_assessment.mitigation: Hedge energy exposure via WDS.AX/WLE.AX; monitor Brent crude; diversify away from oil-import-dependent sectors

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Property credit contraction and developer insolvencies
risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce REIT and property developer exposure; monitor bank NPL disclosures; favour cash-rich balance sheets

risk_assessment.risk_factor: RBA hawkish pivot / rate expectations spike
risk_assessment.mitigation: Favour short-duration bonds; reduce growth equity beta; monitor CPI and RBA communications
Avoid QAN.AX near-term; monitor industrial relations; consider travel alternatives impact on WES.AX
Rotate from pure iron ore (FMG.AX) to diversified miners (BHP.AX) or gold/rare earths
Avoid STAR.AX and distressed property developers; monitor auditor reports across ASX

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gold and rare earths miners amid strategic minerals demand and exploration momentum
opportunities.rationale: Multiple WA/NT projects advancing (Great Southern, Kaiser, Lindian, Barkly) signal sector re-rating; geopolitical risk supports gold

opportunities.recommendation: Tactical long on oil majors on Hormuz disruption premium
opportunities.rationale: US strikes on Iran and Hormuz control uncertainty support Brent above $90; WDS.AX and WLE.AX benefit directly

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight large-cap banks on rising rate expectations supporting NIMs
opportunities.rationale: Rate expectations rocket; CBA.AX and NAB.AX benefit from wider spreads despite property NPL risk

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce REIT and property developer exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: Home values declining, buyer activity at lows, auction sentiment collapsing, Bathla near insolvency, investor credit crashing

defensive_moves.recommendation: Avoid QAN.AX and STAR.AX pending resolution
defensive_moves.rationale: Qantas strike vote creates operational uncertainty; Star faces auditor going-concern doubt with $307m loss

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hedge portfolio with quality defensives and cash
defensive_moves.rationale: Elevated geopolitical risk, property stress, and rate uncertainty warrant reduced equity beta

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain under pressure from oil-driven inflation fears, property sector contagion, and Qantas strike risk. ^AXJO may test support as rate expectations rise. Oil names outperform; property and consumer discretionary lag. Volatility elevated on Hormuz headlines.
market_outlook.long_term: 6–12 month outlook cautious: property credit cycle correction may extend into 2027, pressuring banks' asset quality. Strategic minerals (rare earths, gold, uranium) offer structural upside. AI adoption gap could widen if policy doesn't accelerate. Energy transition fragmented by political gridlock.
